writing.sample_en:
【参考范文 · 162 词】写作无唯一标准答案，以下为达标示范
Living in an increasingly competitive world, college students should better prepare themselves to confront various challenges. This preparation is no longer optional but essential, for those who wait passively will inevitably be left behind.
To begin with, students ought to equip themselves with solid knowledge and practical skills rather than merely chasing high marks. For instance, in today's fierce job market, employers value candidates who can communicate, cooperate and solve real problems. What is more, developing a resilient mindset matters just as much. I still remember failing my first internship interview; instead of giving up, I reflected on my weaknesses, practised repeatedly, and finally secured a position the next semester. That experience taught me that challenges are conquered by those who keep improving.
Therefore, it is high time that college students stopped drifting and started planning ahead. By strengthening both our abilities and our willpower, we can turn the pressure of competition into a driving force and stride confidently into the future.

cloze.title: 2025年12月·第3套 英语六级完形填空（选词填空） · 26–35 题答案与解析

passages.en: It's best to think of an accent as a distinct, systematic and rule-governed way of speaking. Accent is not a __(26)__ for dialect, but it's related. Dialect is an umbrella term for the way a community pronounces words, creates words, and orders words; accent refers to that first part only.
passages.zh: 最好把口音理解为一种独特的、系统的、受规则支配的说话方式。口音并不是方言的同义词，但二者有关联。方言是一个总称，指一个群体发音、造词和排列词语的方式；口音只涉及其中的第一部分。

passages.en: Many __(27)__ presume that there is a single standard way of speaking in each country, with one single standard accent, and that this perceived standard is __(28)__ the best form of speech, but linguists(语言学家) often point out that the concept of a standard accent is better understood as an ideal rather than a __(29)__ . In other words, no one speaks "standard English"; rather, it is an imagined way of using language that exists only in grammar and style books.
passages.zh: 许多普通人想当然地认为，每个国家都有一种单一的标准说话方式和一种单一的标准口音，而且这种被认为是标准的形式在本质上就是最好的说话形式。但语言学家常常指出，标准口音这一概念最好被理解为一种理想，而非现实。换句话说，没有人真正使用“标准英语”；相反，这是一种想象中的语言使用方式，只存在于语法书和文体书中。

passages.en: One reason linguists agree there is no one true standard is that, through the years, there have been __(30)__ supposed standards, depending on time and place. The standard for English in British newsreels(新闻片) from the 1950s, for example, differs greatly from the standard found on American national news broadcasts today. In fact, there has never been a single standard that's been fully agreed upon — and broadcast outlets across the __(31)__ have never consistently held to those standards anyway.
passages.zh: 语言学家之所以同意不存在唯一真正的标准，其中一个原因是，多年来所谓的标准一直不止一个，并且因时间和地点而异。例如，20世纪50年代英国新闻片中的英语标准，与如今美国全国新闻广播中所体现的标准有很大不同。事实上，从来没有一个得到完全一致认可的单一标准，而且各类广播机构也从未始终如一地遵守这些标准。

passages.en: Even so, this idea of a standard accent is __(32)__ and many workplace and educational environments perpetuate the idea that accents that __(33)__ from the current standard are less appropriate, or even inappropriate. Scholars have found that southern US accent features are more accepted in __(34)__ such as government, law and service-oriented workplaces, but less accepted in the technology sector. The acceptability of nonstandard accents may __(35)__ with differences in class and culture, with newer or higher prestige industries expecting more standard speech in the workplace.
passages.zh: 即便如此，标准口音这一观念仍然具有很大影响力，许多工作和教育环境都在延续这样一种观念：偏离当前标准的口音不太合适，甚至是不合适的。学者发现，美国南部口音的特征在政府、法律和服务型工作场所等领域更容易被接受，但在技术行业中则较不受接受。非标准口音的可接受程度可能与阶级和文化差异相关，因为较新或声望更高的行业往往要求员工在工作场所使用更加标准的语言。

rows.text: N) synonym名词
不定冠词 a 后 + for 介词框架

a synonym for 固定搭配 原文 Accent is not a __(26)__ for dialect, but it's related. Dialect is an umbrella term...; accent refers to that first part only. 说"accent 不是 dialect 的 ___，但相关"，紧接着解释 dialect 是包含 accent 的更大范畴——也就是两者不是同义词。a synonym for X 即"X 的同义词"，是英语中固定搭配，语义与逻辑双合。

L)specimen样品义不合语境 specimen 指"标本、样品"，说"accent 不是 dialect 的样品"逻辑不通，且无 a specimen for 这一搭配。 J)reality现实义与对比关系不符 reality 指"现实"，原文是在做术语对比（accent 与 dialect），并非讨论虚实，且 a reality for 在此搭配生硬。 M)spectrum范围义无法对应同义对比 spectrum 指"范围、谱系"，与下文"二者相关但不重合"的同义/上下位对比不匹配。 D)domains复数形式不匹配冠词 a domains 为复数，与不定冠词 a 不兼容；语义"领域"也不构成 accent 与 dialect 的术语对照。 G)laymen复数且指人，不合语境 laymen 为复数指"外行人"，与 a 不搭，且整句是在定义术语，非指代人群。 I)properties复数且抽象属性义偏移 properties 复数与 a 不兼容；"属性"也无法解释 accent 与 dialect 的术语关系。
G) laymen名词
形容词 Many 后 + 之后为谓语动词 presume

外行人对应"想当然以为"的认知主体 Many laymen presume… 即"许多外行人想当然以为……"，恰好与下半句 but linguists(语言学家) often point out that the concept of a standard accent is better understood as an ideal rather than a __(29)__ 中的 linguists 构成"外行 vs 专家"对照，逻辑严丝合缝。
D)domains领域无法做"以为"的主体 domains 指"领域"，是抽象范畴，不能作 presume 的逻辑主语；且与下句 linguists 的对照对象不符。 I)properties属性无法做"以为"的主体 properties 指"属性、财产"，同样是抽象概念，无法 presume；与对照结构不匹配。
F) inherently副词
be 动词与表语形容词之间的修饰位

本质上即最佳，对应"理想型"叙述 原文 Many __(27)__ presume that there is a single standard way of speaking in each country, with one single standard accent, and that this perceived standard is __(28)__ the best form of speech 描述"外行人以为感知到的标准在本质上就是最佳说话方式"，inherently 表"本质上、生来就是"，正好对应这种被想当然的本体论断言。
K)reciprocally相互义与单向断言不符 reciprocally 表"相互地"，需双向主体；句中只是单方面"被认为是最佳"，无相互关系可言。
最具迷惑性的错误词是 K) —— 副词类目仅二选一，词义辨义易翻车。F) inherently 与 K) reciprocally 同为副词，考生若只看到"副词"就随手填，可能误选 reciprocally；防坑：be + ___ + the best form of speech 这种单向断言句不存在"相互"关系，必须看断言方向再选副词。
J) reality名词
rather than 后并列名词位

an ideal rather than a reality 标准口音"更适合被理解为一种理想，而不是现实"，ideal 与 reality 是英语中最经典的反义对子；紧接的下一句 no one speaks "standard English"; rather, it is an imagined way of using language that exists only in grammar and style books. 用"想象的、只存在于语法书中"再次坐实"非现实"，对照成立。

L)specimen样品义与理想无反义对应 specimen 指"样本、标本"，与 ideal 不构成对照，且语义上说"标准口音是样本"不通。 M)spectrum范围义与理想不对仗 spectrum 指"频谱、范围"，与 ideal 既无反义、也不切下句"想象的语言用法"语境。 I)properties复数与 a 不兼容 properties 复数，违背 a + 单数名词 的语法约束；语义"属性"也不构成与 ideal 的对照。
H) multiple形容词
there have been + 空 + 复数名词

多个标准支撑"无统一"论点 本段中心是"语言学家认为没有唯一真标准"，紧跟的例子 The standard for English in British newsreels(新闻片) from the 1950s, for example, differs greatly from the standard found on American national news broadcasts today. 用"50 年代英国 vs 当下美国"佐证存在多个标准，multiple supposed standards 切中要害。
O)unanimous一致同意与无统一标准矛盾 unanimous 表"一致同意的"，若说"存在一致同意的标准"，与下文 there has never been a single standard that's been fully agreed upon 直接打架。
M) spectrum名词
the + 空 + 介词短语
across the spectrum 全谱系 across the spectrum 是英语固定搭配，表"涵盖各种类型/全谱系"。原文意为"全谱系的广播机构都没有始终如一地坚持那些标准"，正好支持"标准并未统一遵行"的主旨。
L)specimen标本义无范围义 specimen 指"标本、样品"，不能表"涵盖范围"，across the specimen 不成立搭配。
E) influential形容词
be 动词后的表语位置

有影响力解释后文延续效应 下文 and many workplace and educational environments perpetuate the idea that accents that __(33)__ from the current standard are less appropriate 说许多职场和教育环境仍在延续这一观念——也就是这一观念"颇有影响力"，influential 正好统摄后文这一果。

O)unanimous一致同意与全文论点冲突 全文反复强调没有统一公认的标准（there has never been a single standard that's been fully agreed upon），若说"标准口音的观念是一致同意的"，与上下文直接矛盾。 H)multiple多个无法搭配单数主语属性 multiple 表"多种的"，用于修饰可数复数或集合概念；说"this idea is multiple"语义不通。

最具迷惑性的错误词是 O) —— unanimous 看着切题，实则与主旨反向。32 题 this idea of a standard accent is ___ 看见"标准口音"主题，部分考生顺势填 unanimous；防坑：联读后文 and many workplace and educational environments perpetuate the idea，重点是"延续/影响"不是"一致同意"，influential 才对得上。
C) deviate动词
that 从句中缺谓语 + 后接 from
deviate from 偏离当前标准 原文整段在讨论"偏离当下标准的口音被视为不合适"，deviate from the current standard 即"偏离当前标准"，词义、搭配、逻辑三处合一。
D) domains名词
介词 in 后 + such as 举例
领域作为政府/法律/服务业的上位词 government、law、service-oriented workplaces 都是社会职业"领域"，domains 表"领域、范围"正是这些行业的自然上位范畴，搭配 in domains such as ___ 在学术英语里极为常见。
I)properties属性义无法囊括行业举例 properties 表"属性、财产"，government 等并非"属性"，无法做其上位范畴；搭配 in properties such as government 语义不通。
B) correlate动词
情态动词 may 后 + 介词 with
correlate with 与……相关联 correlate with 表"与……相关联"，原句意为"非标准口音的可接受度可能与阶层和文化差异相关"，紧跟的 with newer or higher prestige industries expecting more standard speech in the workplace 进一步说明这种相关性的具体表现，逻辑顺畅。

longreading.title: 2025年12月·第3套 英语六级长篇阅读（信息匹配） 第 1 篇 · 36–45 题答案与解析

passages.en: A) Timed traffic lights are set according to schedules that are supposed to coordinate with peak traffic hours. Cities need to monitor and update signal light time schedules at least every two years to keep these systems effective. In Los Angeles, California, an ambitious project to go a step further and synchronize(使同步) every red light in Los Angeles cost over 400 million dollars. Ask a resident of the city and they are likely to agree that saving time on the road is well worth it. If implemented nationwide, synchronization could shave 10% off traffic congestion(堵塞) and 20% off air pollution. Congestion costs time, money, and lives. Big data can help improve how millions of people safely share the road. However, none of this would be possible without the traffic light!
passages.zh: 定时交通信号灯按照应与交通高峰时段相协调的时间表进行设置。城市至少每两年需要监测并更新一次信号灯时间表，以使这些系统保持有效。在加利福尼亚州洛杉矶，一项更进一步、旨在使洛杉矶每一盏红灯同步的雄心勃勃的工程耗资超过4亿美元。问问这座城市的居民，他们很可能会同意，在道路上节省时间是完全值得的。如果在全国范围内实施，同步信号灯可以使交通拥堵减少10%，使空气污染减少20%。拥堵会耗费时间、金钱，甚至夺走生命。大数据能够帮助改善数百万人安全共享道路的方式。然而，如果没有交通信号灯，这一切都不可能实现！

passages.en: B) The first traffic light was invented in London in the 1860's, but it was hardly recognizable — or effective. It had been adapted from the railroad signal system by a railway manager, John Peak Knight, in 1868. The railroads used red gas lights at night to signal stops and green gas lights during the daytime. Knight installed a similar gas light, semaphore(臂板信号) system near London's Westminster Bridge in December of 1868.
passages.zh: 第一盏交通信号灯于19世纪60年代在伦敦发明，但它很难被辨认出来，也几乎没有效果。1868年，铁路经理约翰·皮克·奈特将铁路信号系统改造后发明了它。铁路在夜间使用红色煤气灯表示停车，白天使用绿色煤气灯。1868年12月，奈特在伦敦威斯敏斯特桥附近安装了一个类似的煤气灯臂板信号系统。

passages.en: C) The life of the first traffic light signal was short-lived. A gas leak caused one of the signal lights to explode on its police officer operator within a month of being installed.
passages.zh: 第一盏交通信号灯的使用寿命很短。安装不到一个月，一次煤气泄漏导致其中一盏信号灯在负责操作它的警察身上爆炸。

passages.en: D) Automating traffic signals stalled after the London incident. Forty years passed before cars crowding city streets urged the development of traffic lights in the United States. London would not see another traffic light until 1929.
passages.zh: 伦敦事件之后，交通信号的自动化进程陷入停滞。四十年过去，城市街道上拥挤的汽车促使美国开始研制交通信号灯。直到1929年，伦敦才再次出现交通信号灯。

passages.en: E) The United States is a car culture like no other country. Unlike most European cities that started urban planning when horses were high-tech, many cities in the United States were designed around urban sprawl, suburban tracts, and motor cars.
passages.zh: 美国是世界上独一无二的汽车文化国家。与大多数在马匹还属于高科技时就开始进行城市规划的欧洲城市不同，美国的许多城市是围绕城市蔓延、郊区地块和机动车设计的。

passages.en: F) As traffic and cities grew, so did the race to solve growing traffic problems. The first traffic signals were semaphores. Semaphores are towers with moving arms signaling for traffic to stop or go. They could be manual or automatic. There was no consistent design. Various models were invented and put into place in cities as the need arose.
passages.zh: 随着交通和城市的发展，解决日益严重的交通问题的竞争也愈演愈烈。最早的交通信号是臂板信号。臂板信号是带有活动臂的塔，通过活动臂发出让交通停下或通行的信号。它们可以手动操作，也可以自动运行。当时没有统一的设计。随着需求出现，各种型号被发明出来并应用于各个城市。

passages.en: G) In 1912, Lester Wire was a police officer exhausted by traffic at Main Street and 200 South. He developed a manually switched stop light. The four-sided box, raised on a ten-foot pole, looked like a birdhouse and was operated manually by an officer. The officer would flip a switch to change between the dipped red and green lights.
passages.zh: 1912年，莱斯特·怀尔是一名警察，他因缅因街与南200街交叉口的交通状况而疲惫不堪。于是，他研制出一种手动切换的停车灯。这个四面盒子被架在一根十英尺高的杆子上，外形像一个鸟舍，由警察手动操作。警察拨动开关，在暗红灯和绿灯之间切换。

passages.en: H) Like the 1910 semaphore, the first electric signal used words. However, the words were no longer written on arms that raised and fell. The words "stop" or "move" were on lights. The posts lit up on each of four corner-posts around an intersection(十字路口). It was not automated, though. A booth with an operator was required to flip the switches.
passages.zh: 与1910年的臂板信号一样，第一种电动信号也使用文字。不过，文字不再写在上下移动的臂板上，而是显示在灯上。十字路口四个角落的立柱上都亮起“停”或“行”字样。但它并非自动运行，仍需要一个设有操作员的岗亭来拨动开关。

passages.en: I) The system allowed police officers to move from the middle of the street to a corner. From that vantage(有利地位), an officer could oversee the crowd. If an emergency vehicle came, the officer could flip a switch and clear the intersection by triggering all red lights. The emergency vehicle could now pass effortlessly. Finally, in San Francisco the first red and green electric light system that could be operated automatically (or manually) was introduced in 1917.
passages.zh: 这一系统使警察能够从街道中央转移到街角。从那个有利位置，警察可以监视人群。如果有应急车辆到来，警察可以拨动开关，使所有信号灯变红，从而清空十字路口。应急车辆便可以轻松通过。最终，1917年，旧金山引入了第一套可以自动运行（也可以手动操作）的红绿电灯系统。

passages.en: J) In 1920, the first three-color light system was introduced in Detroit — also known as Motor City, USA. The evolution of traffic light signals could not have a more appropriate context than Motor City. Ford Motor Company was founded in Detroit in 1903 (and other motor companies followed). Ford made cars affordable for more common people, rather than the wealthy, by creating larger scale factory production.
passages.zh: 1920年，第一套三色信号灯系统在底特律投入使用，这座城市也被称为美国的“汽车城”。交通信号灯的发展没有比“汽车城”更合适的背景了。福特汽车公司于1903年在底特律成立（其他汽车公司随后也相继成立）。福特通过大规模工厂化生产，使汽车变得更加普通的人也买得起，而不再只是富人的消费品。

passages.en: K) Stop and go were insufficient for the new volumes of cars zooming through intersections. Streets were full of new numbers of cars in addition to delivery wagons, bustling crowds, bicycles, horse-drawn carriages, and street cars. The introduction of the cautionary yellow light helped increase driver safety, decreasing accidents that come from running red lights.
passages.zh: 对于大量新汽车飞驰通过十字路口的情况，仅有停车和通行两种信号已经不够了。街道上除了送货马车外，还挤满了数量不断增加的汽车、熙攘的人群、自行车、马车和有轨电车。警示性黄灯的引入提高了驾驶员的安全性，减少了因闯红灯而发生的事故。

passages.en: L) Stop lights were incredibly important in chaotic city streets. Crosswalks weren't even introduced until 1951. The first pedestrian fatality in the United States was in 1899.
passages.zh: 在混乱的城市街道上，停车灯极其重要。直到1951年，人行横道才被引入。美国第一起行人死亡事故发生于1899年。

passages.en: M) The development of the modern traffic light may have started in London, but it grew up in the United States. In Cleveland, an African-American inventor named Garrett Morgan came up with an affordable, patented traffic signal. The yellow light made intersections safer than the old stop and go system. The new design was inexpensive enough that it allowed the installation of a lot more lights.
passages.zh: 现代交通信号灯的发展或许始于伦敦，但它是在美国发展成熟的。在克利夫兰，一位名叫加勒特·摩根的非裔美国发明家发明了一种价格实惠并获得专利的交通信号灯。黄灯使十字路口比旧式的停车和通行系统更加安全。这种新设计成本低廉，因此可以安装更多信号灯。

passages.en: N) Morgan sold the patent to General Electric — and the spread of the traffic light was green lighted. Green means go. It is that simple, but it's still best to check both ways for oncoming traffic that may not be paying attention or is running the light. Yellow means slow down and prepare to stop. It does not mean full-throttle(全速) ahead. While you may get away with gunning it into the intersection, running a yellow can lead to tickets and dangerous accidents. Red lights are a clear and consistent warning to stop. Even where right turns are allowed on red lights, you must come to a complete stop before turning right. You must also yield to any through traffic, which has the right of way. In most states and cities, you can take a right on red unless otherwise indicated. New York City does not allow a right on red.
passages.zh: 摩根将专利卖给了通用电气公司，交通信号灯的普及也因此获得了绿灯。绿灯表示通行。道理很简单，但你仍然最好向两边查看，因为迎面而来的车辆可能没有注意信号灯，或者正在闯灯。黄灯表示减速并准备停车，并不意味着可以全速前进。虽然你可能侥幸加速驶入十字路口而不被追究，但闯黄灯可能会导致罚单和危险事故。红灯是明确而统一的停车警告。即使红灯时允许右转，右转前也必须完全停车。你还必须让行所有直行车辆，因为它们拥有先行权。在大多数州和城市，除非另有标示，红灯时可以右转。纽约市不允许红灯时右转。

passages.en: O) Red arrows mean you cannot turn right on a red in most states. The green arrow, in these cases, is the only time you can make the turn. However, you can take a right on a red arrow after a full stop in the states of Illinois, Kansas, Louisiana, Maryland, Michigan, New Hampshire, North Dakota, Oregon, South Carolina, Utah, Washington State and Wyoming.
passages.zh: 在大多数州，红色箭头表示红灯时不能右转。在这些情况下，只有绿箭头亮起时才能转弯。不过，在伊利诺伊州、堪萨斯州、路易斯安那州、马里兰州、密歇根州、新罕布什尔州、北达科他州、俄勒冈州、南卡罗来纳州、犹他州、华盛顿州和怀俄明州，红色箭头时完全停车后可以右转。

passages.en: P) Flashing Red is the same as a stop sign, generally used at four-way intersections where there is minimal traffic. When arriving at a flashing red light, make a full and complete stop. Flashing Red Arrows similarly mean to stop and then proceed to take the turn. Flashing Yellow lights mean yield or signal caution, like outside of a fire station. There are no all-direction flashing yellow lights, since it is prohibited in the United States. If you have a flashing yellow light, you are to yield to oncoming traffic.
passages.zh: 闪烁的红灯通常等同于停车标志，一般用于交通量很小的四向交叉路口。到达闪烁红灯处时，要完全停车。闪烁的红色箭头同样表示停车，然后再继续转弯。闪烁的黄灯表示让行或注意警示，例如消防站外的信号灯。美国禁止设置全方向闪烁黄灯，因此不存在这种信号。如果你遇到闪烁的黄灯，就必须让行迎面而来的车辆。

passages.en: Q) Flashing Yellow Arrows are part of a four-signal traffic light. These are used in some states after a protected green turn signal, or arrow, but before a steady yellow arrow. When a flashing yellow arrow is shown, you can take the turn after yielding to pedestrians and traffic. Steady Yellow Arrows maintain the normal yellow light caution in three-light signals, meaning to stop or prepare to stop. In a four-signal system that has a flashing yellow arrow, the steady yellow arrow is a signal that the yield period is ending. The red arrow is about to start. Vehicles should stop if safely possible. Traffic tickets are possible for running a steady yellow arrow.
passages.zh: 闪烁的黄色箭头是四信号灯交通信号的一部分。在一些州，这种信号灯设置在受保护的绿灯转弯信号或箭头之后、稳定的黄色箭头之前。出现闪烁的黄色箭头时，在让行行人和车辆后可以转弯。稳定的黄色箭头在三信号灯系统中保持普通黄灯的警示含义，即停车或准备停车。在设有闪烁黄色箭头的四信号灯系统中，稳定的黄色箭头表示让行阶段即将结束，红色箭头即将亮起。如果安全可行，车辆应停车。闯过稳定的黄色箭头可能会收到交通罚单。

passages.en: R) Traffic light meaning is fairly consistent across the board with various deviations. Green means it's safe to proceed (though you should still exercise caution). Yellow means caution and yield. Red means danger and stop. Always drive defensively and obey traffic signals.
passages.zh: 尽管存在各种差异，交通信号灯的含义总体上相当一致。绿灯表示可以安全通行（不过仍应保持谨慎）。黄灯表示注意并让行。红灯表示危险并停车。始终采取防御性驾驶，并遵守交通信号。

statements.en: Upon seeing a flashing yellow arrow, a driver should let pedestrians and traffic pass first before taking the turn.
statements.zh: 看到闪烁的黄色箭头时,驾驶员应该先让行人和车辆通过,然后再转弯。

analysis.锚点: 闪烁黄色箭头 + 先让行后转弯
analysis.定位: Q 段 When a flashing yellow arrow is shown, you can take the turn after yielding to pedestrians and traffic. 出现闪烁的黄色箭头时，你可以在先给行人和过往车辆让行之后再转弯。
analysis.改写: flashing yellow arrow↔flashing yellow arrow 术语原样复现 let pedestrians and traffic pass first before taking the turn↔you can take the turn after yielding to pedestrians and traffic yield = 让行的同义改写
analysis.辨邻: P P 段同样出现 flashing yellow 等词，但讨论的是 Flashing Yellow lights mean yield or signal caution 这类整盏闪黄灯，没有提“先让行后转弯”这一动作链条，所以不是题 36 的源头段。 Flashing Yellow lights mean yield or signal caution, like outside of a fire station

statements.en: The red and green automatic traffic light system originated in an American city.
statements.zh: 红绿灯自动交通信号系统起源于一个美国城市。

analysis.锚点: 首套自动红绿信号 + 美国城市
analysis.定位: I 段 Finally, in San Francisco the first red and green electric light system that could be operated automatically (or manually) was introduced in 1917. 最后，在旧金山，首套可自动（或手动）运行的红绿电灯系统于 1917 年问世。
analysis.改写: red and green automatic traffic light system↔the first red and green electric light system that could be operated automatically (or manually) automatic 与 automatically 同根改写 originated in an American city↔in San Francisco 下位地名替上位描述
analysis.辨邻: J J 段同样讲美国城市 Detroit 与首次出现，但所述是 the first three-color light system 而非题干的 “red and green automatic”，少了“两色 + 自动”这关键限定，覆盖不全。 In 1920, the first three-color light system was introduced in Detroit G G 段虽也讲红绿灯 between the dipped red and green lights，但明确说 operated manually by an officer，不是 automatic，故不是题 37 源头段。 He developed a manually switched stop light

statements.en: Residents of an American city tend to share the opinion that time saved on the road justifies the cost of upgrading its traffic light system.
statements.zh: 一个美国城市的居民倾向于认为在道路上节省的时间证明升级其交通信号系统的成本是合理的。

analysis.锚点: 美国某市居民认为省时间值回升级成本
analysis.定位: A 段 Ask a resident of the city and they are likely to agree that saving time on the road is well worth it. 你去问问这座城市的居民，他们多半会同意：在路上省下的时间，绝对值回投入。
analysis.改写: Residents of an American city tend to share the opinion↔Ask a resident of the city and they are likely to agree 复数与单数态度的同义改写 time saved on the road justifies the cost of upgrading its traffic light system↔saving time on the road is well worth it well worth it = 物有所值

statements.en: Mass production of cars made it possible for ordinary people to buy them.
statements.zh: 汽车的大规模生产使普通人能够购买汽车。

analysis.锚点: 汽车的大规模生产让普通人买得起
analysis.定位: J 段 Ford made cars affordable for more common people, rather than the wealthy, by creating larger scale factory production. 福特通过创立更大规模的工厂生产，使汽车不再只属于富人，而是变成普通人也买得起的东西。
analysis.改写: Mass production of cars↔creating larger scale factory production 工厂规模化生产 = 大规模生产 made it possible for ordinary people to buy them↔made cars affordable for more common people, rather than the wealthy affordable = made it possible to buy
analysis.辨邻: E E 段虽提及 The United States is a car culture like no other country 等汽车扩张背景，但并未陈述“大规模生产让普通人买得起汽车”这一具体机制。 many cities in the United States were designed around urban sprawl, suburban tracts, and motor cars

statements.en: What a traffic light means is almost the same everywhere despite some variations.
statements.zh: 尽管存在一些差异,交通信号灯的含义在各地几乎相同。

analysis.锚点: 信号灯含义到处几乎一样、有些差异
analysis.定位: R 段 Traffic light meaning is fairly consistent across the board with various deviations. 总体来看，红绿灯的含义大体上保持一致，只是存在一些差异。
analysis.改写: almost the same everywhere↔fairly consistent across the board across the board = everywhere despite some variations↔with various deviations with = despite 的让步同义

statements.en: Pedestrian crossings came into being only in the mid-twentieth century.
statements.zh: 人行横道仅在二十世纪中叶才出现。

analysis.锚点: 人行横道仅在 20 世纪中叶才出现
analysis.定位: L 段 Crosswalks weren't even introduced until 1951. 人行横道甚至直到 1951 年才出现。
analysis.改写: Pedestrian crossings↔Crosswalks 同义词替换 came into being only in the mid-twentieth century↔weren't even introduced until 1951 until 1951 = 直到 20 世纪中叶才

statements.en: People raced to address increasing traffic problems along with the expansion of cities and traffic.
statements.zh: 随着城市和交通的扩张,人们竞相解决日益严重的交通问题。

analysis.锚点: 城市与交通扩张 + 解决交通问题的竞赛
analysis.定位: F 段 As traffic and cities grew, so did the race to solve growing traffic problems. 随着交通和城市的扩张，解决日益严重的交通问题的竞赛也愈演愈烈。
analysis.改写: People raced to address increasing traffic problems↔so did the race to solve growing traffic problems race + address ≈ race + solve along with the expansion of cities and traffic↔As traffic and cities grew expansion 是 grew 的名词化

statements.en: When the warning yellow light was introduced, driving became safer and traffic accidents reduced.
statements.zh: 当黄色警告灯被引入时,驾驶变得更加安全,交通事故减少了。

analysis.锚点: 黄灯被引入后驾驶更安全、事故减少
analysis.定位: K 段 The introduction of the cautionary yellow light helped increase driver safety, decreasing accidents that come from running red lights. 警示性黄灯的引入帮助提高了驾驶者的安全，减少了因闯红灯导致的事故。
analysis.改写: the warning yellow light was introduced↔The introduction of the cautionary yellow light warning = cautionary 同义形容词 driving became safer and traffic accidents reduced↔helped increase driver safety, decreasing accidents increase driver safety = 驾驶变安全；decreasing = reduced

statements.en: The signal system on the railroad served as the basis for the first traffic light.
statements.zh: 铁路上的信号系统是第一个交通信号灯的基础。

analysis.锚点: 铁路信号系统是首盏红绿灯的基础
analysis.定位: B 段 It had been adapted from the railroad signal system by a railway manager, John Peak Knight, in 1868. 它是 1868 年由铁路经理 John Peak Knight 仿照铁路信号系统改造而来的。
analysis.改写: The signal system on the railroad↔the railroad signal system of/on 与定语顺序的等价 served as the basis for the first traffic light↔It had been adapted from the railroad signal system adapted from = served as the basis for
analysis.辨邻: F F 段把最早信号灯描述为 The first traffic signals were semaphores，并没有提到 “railroad signal system” 作为基础，故不是题 44 源头段。 The first traffic signals were semaphores

statements.en: Even though a green light signals "go", attention should be paid to traffic on either side in case some driver is being careless or ignoring a red light.
statements.zh: 即使绿灯表示"通行",也应注意两侧的交通情况,以防某些驾驶员粗心大意或无视红灯。

analysis.锚点: 绿灯也要留意两侧、防有人闯红
analysis.定位: N 段 Green means go. It is that simple, but it's still best to check both ways for oncoming traffic that may not be paying attention or is running the light. 绿灯表示通行。就这么简单，但最好还是双向都看一下，留意那些可能心不在焉、或者正在闯灯的对向车辆。
analysis.改写: Even though a green light signals "go"↔Green means go. It is that simple “signals go” 与 “means go” 同义 attention should be paid to traffic on either side↔it's still best to check both ways for oncoming traffic both ways = either side，check = pay attention in case some driver is being careless or ignoring a red light↔may not be paying attention or is running the light running the light = ignoring a red light；not paying attention = careless
analysis.辨邻: R R 段虽提及 Green means it's safe to proceed (though you should still exercise caution)，但没有具体说“两侧来车”和“有人闯红灯”，覆盖不到题干这两个关键细节。 Green means it's safe to proceed (though you should still exercise caution)

passages.en: Mindfulness has been shown to have a number of meaningful health benefits — it can help reduce anxiety and promote healing in those suffering from chronic illness.
passages.zh: 研究表明，正念具有多项显著的健康益处——它有助于减轻焦虑，促进慢性病患者的康复。

passages.en: The practice is based on an insight first described in ancient Buddhist texts that human beings have the capacity to observe experience without being caught up in it. This means simply that it is possible to observe ourselves having a craving, or a happy thought, or even a scary emotion, without reacting in the moment in a way that amplifies the feeling or sends the mind spiraling off into thinking about old memories or anticipating events.
passages.zh: 这种练习建立在古代佛教典籍中最早阐述的一种洞见之上，即人类有能力观察自身的体验，而不被其牵着走。这简单地意味着，我们可以观察自己正在产生欲望、思绪愉快，甚至感到恐惧，却不在当下做出会强化这种感受的反应，也不让头脑陷入回忆往事或预想未来的思绪之中。

passages.en: This practice of mindfulness can help calm the mind and the body as we learn not to react to experience with likes and dislikes or judgments of good and bad. It does not make us cold or indifferent but more fully present.
passages.zh: 随着我们学会不以喜欢和不喜欢，或好与坏的评判来回应体验，正念练习能够帮助我们平静心灵和身体。它不会使我们变得冷漠或无动于衷，反而会让我们更加充分地活在当下。

passages.en: One of the challenges of practicing mindfulness in our contemporary world is that there has been a profound transformation in human attention. The artist Jenny Odell argues that in our "attention economy" human attention has been transformed into a commodity that big corporations buy and sell. This economy rests on a technological revolution of mobile phones and social media that makes it possible for corporations to target our attention with their content at every moment.
passages.zh: 在当今世界练习正念所面临的挑战之一，是人类的注意力已经发生了深刻的转变。艺术家珍妮·奥德尔认为，在我们的“注意力经济”中，人类的注意力已经被转化为一种由大公司买卖的商品。这种经济建立在手机和社交媒体的技术革命之上，使公司能够随时利用其内容来吸引我们的注意力。

passages.en: The devices most people use are a perpetual diversion from the present moment. The result is that it can feel as though our ability to focus, and be fully present, has been stolen. But mindfulness can help us resist the attention economy and relish the things that make life special, like being together with those we love.
passages.zh: 大多数人使用的设备不断把我们从当下分散开来。结果是，我们可能会觉得自己集中注意力并充分活在当下的能力被夺走了。但正念能够帮助我们抵制注意力经济，享受那些使生活变得特别的事物，比如与我们所爱的人相聚。

passages.en: Most mindfulness research focuses on the individual benefits of the practice, but some scholars assert that we can not only practice mindfulness for ourselves but also practice it for others. It can help us build stronger, healthier relationships.
passages.zh: 大多数关于正念的研究都集中于这种练习对个人的益处，但一些学者认为，我们不仅可以为自己练习正念，也可以为他人练习正念。它能够帮助我们建立更牢固、更健康的人际关系。

passages.en: The sad truth is that living in the attention economy, most of us have become bad listeners. However, just as it is possible to watch ourselves having an experience without reacting, it's possible to watch another person have an experience without getting tied up in reactivity and judgment.
passages.zh: 令人悲哀的事实是，生活在注意力经济中的我们大多数人都已经不善于倾听。然而，正如我们可以观察自己正在经历某种体验而不做出反应一样，我们也可以观察另一个人正在经历某种体验，而不陷入情绪反应和评判之中。

passages.en: The gift of mindfulness is a practice of listening with compassion to others describe their experiences. To give this gift means putting away your phone, turning off social media, and setting aside other common distractions. It means practicing being fully present in another person's presence and listening to them with complete attention without judgment, while resisting the urge to make the interaction about you.
passages.zh: 正念的馈赠，是带着同情心倾听他人描述自己的经历。要送出这份礼物，就意味着收起手机，关闭社交媒体，并把其他常见的干扰放到一边。这意味着练习在他人面前完全保持当下，以全部注意力、不带评判地倾听对方，同时克制住把这次互动变成谈论自己的冲动。

passages.en: If we judge the value of gifts based on their price, this gift may seem worthless, but in a distracted world, it is a precious one.
passages.zh: 如果我们根据礼物的价格来判断其价值，那么这份礼物可能显得一文不值；但在一个注意力分散的世界里，它却是一份珍贵的礼物。

questions.stem: What do we learn from the passage about practicing mindfulness?
questions.stem_zh: 从文章中我们了解到关于练习正念的什么内容?

options.text: It triggers our mind to reflect on past experiences or anticipate future events.
options.zh: 它触发我们的思维去反思过去的经历或预期未来的事件。

options.text: It focuses our attention on the present moment without making judgments.
options.zh: 它将我们的注意力集中在当下时刻而不做评判。

options.text: It concentrates our mind on our personal feelings, happy or scary.
options.zh: 它将我们的思维集中在个人感受上,无论是快乐的还是恐惧的。

options.text: It helps our mind to stay calm when facing judgments from others.
options.zh: 它帮助我们的思维在面对他人的评判时保持平静。

questions.判型: What do we learn from the passage about practicing mindfulness 问的是文章关于 mindfulness 的客观陈述，没有 infer/imply/mainly 这类信号，是一道关于 mindfulness 本质特征的细节题。
questions.拆句: What do we learn from the passage about practicing mindfulness? 主干是 What do we learn from the passage，about practicing mindfulness 是介词短语后置补充询问对象，结构直白无陷阱。
questions.定位: P2 This means simply that it is possible to observe ourselves having a craving, or a happy thought, or even a scary emotion, without reacting in the moment in a way that amplifies the feeling or sends the mind spiraling off into thinking about old memories or anticipating events. 这意味着，我们可以观察自己产生渴望、愉快念头甚至恐惧情绪，而无需在当下作出反应、不放大该情绪，也不让心思滑向旧时记忆或对未来事件的预期。

locate.en: This means simply that it is possible to observe ourselves having a craving, or a happy thought, or even a scary emotion, without reacting in the moment in a way that amplifies the feeling or sends the mind spiraling off into thinking about old memories or anticipating events.
locate.zh: 这意味着，我们可以观察自己产生渴望、愉快念头甚至恐惧情绪，而无需在当下作出反应、不放大该情绪，也不让心思滑向旧时记忆或对未来事件的预期。

option_analysis.note: 原文 without … sends the mind spiraling off into thinking about old memories or anticipating events 明确把「回想旧事 / 预期未来」放在否定结构里，是正念要避免的，A 把它说成正念的作用，恰好与原文相反。
预判落在「观察当下、不卷入、不评判」三点上，focuses our attention on the present moment without making judgments 把前两点合在一句里全覆盖，是定位句的紧贴改写。

pairs.opt: focuses our attention on the present moment

option_analysis.note: 原文 observe ourselves having a craving, or a happy thought, or even a scary emotion, without reacting in the moment 强调观察情绪而不卷入，C 项却说「把注意力集中在个人情绪上」，把「观察」偷换成「集中」，两者一冷静一沉浸，语义错位。
原文谈的是「自己不对体验作好坏评判」（judgments of good and bad），并未涉及「他人评判我们」，D 项把评判主体从「自我」换成「他人」，无原文依据。

questions.stem: What do we see in today's "attention economy" according to Jenny Odell?
questions.stem_zh: 根据Jenny Odell的说法,我们在当今的"注意力经济"中看到了什么?

options.text: Focus on technological advances continuously updates products and services.
options.zh: 对技术进步的关注持续更新着产品和服务。

options.text: People's attention is turned into something that can be bought and sold.
options.zh: 人们的注意力变成了可以被买卖的东西。

options.text: Businesses profit from selling mobile phones and revolutionizing social media.
options.zh: 企业通过销售手机和革新社交媒体获利。

options.text: People tend to purchase products and services without careful thinking.
options.zh: 人们倾向于不加仔细思考就购买产品和服务。

questions.判型: What do we see in today's attention economy according to Jenny Odell 用 according to 把答案归到 Jenny Odell 名下，是事实归属型细节题。
questions.拆句: What do we see in today's "attention economy" according to Jenny Odell? 主干 What do we see in today's attention economy，according to Jenny Odell 是把观点归属到具体人物的状语，关键在于答案必须落到 Odell 的话上，而不是文章自己说的。
questions.定位: P4 The artist Jenny Odell argues that in our "attention economy" human attention has been transformed into a commodity that big corporations buy and sell. 艺术家 Jenny Odell 论述道：在我们的「注意力经济」中，人的注意力已经被转化成大公司买卖的商品。

locate.en: The artist Jenny Odell argues that in our "attention economy" human attention has been transformed into a commodity that big corporations buy and sell.
locate.zh: 艺术家 Jenny Odell 论述道：在我们的「注意力经济」中，人的注意力已经被转化成大公司买卖的商品。

option_analysis.note: 原文 This economy rests on a technological revolution of mobile phones and social media that makes it possible for corporations to target our attention with their content at every moment 说技术革命让公司能持续抢占注意力，没说技术让产品/服务持续更新，A 项偷换了技术革命的作用。
选项 B 几乎是 Odell 原话的一对一改写，主语、动词、对象、属性四要素全对齐，是 according to 型细节题里最干净的同义替换。

pairs.orig: human attention has been transformed into a commodity that big corporations buy and sell
pairs.opt: People's attention is turned into something that can be bought and sold

option_analysis.note: 原文 buy and sell 的宾语是 human attention（人的注意力），C 项把宾语偷换成 mobile phones and social media，是把抽象对象偷换成具体技术，正好踩中考生「具象更易接受」的认知偏误。
原文谈的是公司买卖「人的注意力」，并未谈消费者本身是否冲动消费；D 项关于「人们购买商品不细想」属凭空生造。

questions.stem: What happens with the prevalent use of mobile phones or social media?
questions.stem_zh: 手机或社交媒体的普遍使用会发生什么?

options.text: They keep distracting users from the here and now.
options.zh: 它们不断使用户从此时此地分心。

options.text: They render users incapable of resisting temptation.
options.zh: 它们使用户无法抵抗诱惑。

options.text: They rob users of their ability to observe experience.
options.zh: 它们剥夺了用户观察体验的能力。

options.text: They tempt users to endorse the attention economy.
options.zh: 它们诱使用户认同注意力经济。

questions.判型: What happens with the prevalent use of mobile phones or social media 直接问 What happens，是问客观结果，属于细节题。
questions.拆句: What happens with the prevalent use of mobile phones or social media? 主干 What happens，with the prevalent use of… 是介词短语作伴随状语，相当于 when… are widely used，结构平实。
questions.定位: P5 The devices most people use are a perpetual diversion from the present moment. 大多数人使用的这些设备是一种让人持续偏离当下的干扰。

locate.en: The devices most people use are a perpetual diversion from the present moment.
locate.zh: 大多数人使用的这些设备是一种让人持续偏离当下的干扰。

option_analysis.note: A 项两个核心语义点（keep distracting、from the here and now）与原文 perpetual diversion、from the present moment 一一对应，是定位句的紧贴改写。

pairs.orig: The devices most people use are a perpetual diversion from the present moment
pairs.opt: They keep distracting users from the here and now

option_analysis.note: 原文 But mindfulness can help us resist the attention economy 谈的是正念能帮我们抵抗，B 项却说设备让用户「彻底失去抵御诱惑的能力」，把「分心」夸大为「丧失抵抗力」，无原文依据。
原文 our ability to focus, and be fully present, has been stolen 谈被偷走的是「专注、全在当下」的能力，而 capacity to observe experience 才是 observe experience 的能力，C 项把两者混在一起，张冠李戴。
原文只说设备让人分心、注意力被卖，没说设备诱使用户主动「支持/认同」注意力经济，D 项凭空多出一个「用户主动认同」的环节。

questions.stem: What benefit can practicing mindfulness bring to us according to some scholars?
questions.stem_zh: 根据一些学者的说法,练习正念能给我们带来什么好处?

options.text: It prevents us from making arbitrary judgments about others.
options.zh: 它防止我们对他人做出武断的评判。

options.text: It shifts our attention from material things to spiritual pursuits.
options.zh: 它将我们的注意力从物质事物转移到精神追求。

options.text: It is conducive to our forging better interpersonal relationships.
options.zh: 它有助于我们建立更好的人际关系。

options.text: It is helpful in regaining our ability to enjoy what we have in life.
options.zh: 它有助于恢复我们享受生活中所拥有之物的能力。

questions.判型: What benefit can practicing mindfulness bring to us according to some scholars 用 according to some scholars 归属信息源，是出处型细节题。
questions.拆句: What benefit can practicing mindfulness bring to us according to some scholars? 主干 What benefit can practicing mindfulness bring to us，according to some scholars 是把观点归到学者群体的状语，注意不要把作者自己其它段落的好处当成学者说的。
questions.定位: P6 Most mindfulness research focuses on the individual benefits of the practice, but some scholars assert that we can not only practice mindfulness for ourselves but also practice it for others. It can help us build stronger, healthier relationships. 多数正念研究关注其个人层面的益处，但一些学者论断：正念不仅可为己练，也可为他人而练；它能帮我们建立更稳固、更健康的人际关系。

locate.en: Most mindfulness research focuses on the individual benefits of the practice, but some scholars assert that we can not only practice mindfulness for ourselves but also practice it for others. It can help us build stronger, healthier relationships.
locate.zh: 多数正念研究关注其个人层面的益处，但一些学者论断：正念不仅可为己练，也可为他人而练；它能帮我们建立更稳固、更健康的人际关系。

option_analysis.note: 「不作评判」是 P3 谈 mindfulness 个体效用时的内容，而 Q49 问的是 some scholars 的观点；把 P3 的句子嫁接到学者名下属于张冠李戴，且 prevent us from making arbitrary judgments about others 也夸大了原文「自己不评判体验」的限定。
原文没有把好处归结为「从物质转向精神追求」，B 项凭空生造一组对立维度。
C 项把学者观点收束句 help us build stronger, healthier relationships 完整改写成 conducive to our forging better interpersonal relationships，主体、动作、对象逐项对齐。

pairs.orig: help us build stronger, healthier relationships
pairs.opt: conducive to our forging better interpersonal relationships

option_analysis.note: 「重拾享受生活的能力」对应 relish the things that make life special, like being together with those we love，是作者自己的论述而非 some scholars 的观点；嫁接到学者名下属于张冠李戴。

questions.stem: What does the author suggest we do in another person's presence?
questions.stem_zh: 作者建议我们在他人面前做什么?

options.text: Share each other's experience frankly and compassionately.
options.zh: 坦诚而富有同情心地分享彼此的经历。

options.text: Pay full attention to establishing close relationships with them.
options.zh: 全神贯注于与他们建立亲密关系。

options.text: Be attentive listeners while refraining from making judgments.
options.zh: 做专注的倾听者同时避免做出评判。

options.text: Remind them of the distraction from mobile phones and social media.
options.zh: 提醒他们注意来自手机和社交媒体的干扰。

questions.判型: What does the author suggest we do in another person's presence 问的是作者对一个具体场景给出的具体做法，是建议型细节题。
questions.拆句: What does the author suggest we do in another person's presence? 主干 What does the author suggest we do，in another person's presence 是地点状语；suggest 后接省略 that 的从句 we do…，注意 suggest 在此为「建议」义、不是「暗示」义。
questions.定位: P8 It means practicing being fully present in another person's presence and listening to them with complete attention without judgment, while resisting the urge to make the interaction about you. 这意味着练习在另一个人面前全然临在，全神贯注地倾听他们，不作评判，同时克制把对话焦点拉回到自己身上的冲动。

locate.en: It means practicing being fully present in another person's presence and listening to them with complete attention without judgment, while resisting the urge to make the interaction about you.
locate.zh: 这意味着练习在另一个人面前全然临在，全神贯注地倾听他们，不作评判，同时克制把对话焦点拉回到自己身上的冲动。

option_analysis.note: 原文 resisting the urge to make the interaction about you 明确要求克制把谈话拉回到「自己」，强调单向倾听对方；A 项却说 share each other's experience 双向分享，与原文要求方向相反。
原文要求把全部注意力放在对方的体验上，目的是「以正念之心送出倾听这一礼物」（practicing being fully present in another person's presence）；B 项却把目的偷换成 establishing close relationships with them——这是 Q49 的话题，且原文未把它定为这一场景的目的。
C 项把作者建议的两项核心动作（with complete attention、without judgment）都直接对应到选项的两个分句，是同义改写最紧贴的一项。

pairs.orig: listening to them with complete attention without judgment
pairs.opt: Be attentive listeners while refraining from making judgments

option_analysis.note: 原文要求自己 putting away your phone, turning off social media, and setting aside other common distractions，即「自己」放下手机，并未要求去提醒对方；D 项把动作主体从「自己」偷换到「提醒他人」，无原文依据。

reading2.title: 2025年12月·第3套 英语六级阅读理解（四选一） 第 2 篇 · 51–55 题答案与解析

passages.en: The other day I had to log into a service I hadn't used before. Since I was a new user, the website decided that it needed to check I wasn't a robot and so set me a Captcha test to determine whether the user is a person or a machine.
passages.zh: 前几天，我不得不登录一个以前从未使用过的服务。由于我是新用户，网站认定有必要确认我不是机器人，于是给我设置了一项验证码测试，以判断用户是人还是机器。

passages.en: I was presented with an image of a roadside scene over which was laid a grid. My "challenge" was to click on each cell in the grid that contained a traffic sign. I did so, a bit irritated. Then I was presented with another image and another grid — also with a request to identify road signs. Like a lamb, I complied, after which the website accepted my input.
passages.zh: 我看到的是一幅道路旁场景的图片，上面覆盖着一个网格。我的“挑战”是点击网格中每一个包含交通标志的单元格。我照做了，心里有些恼火。接着，网站又给我展示了另一幅图片和另一个网格，同样要求我找出道路标志。我像只待宰的羔羊一样照办了，之后网站接受了我的输入。

passages.en: And then I realised what I had been doing was adding to a dataset for training the machine-learning software that guides self-driving cars. So, to gain access to an automated service that will benefit financially from my input, I first have to do some unpaid labor to help improve the performance of autonomous vehicles.
passages.zh: 随后我意识到，我刚才所做的一切，实际上是在为训练自动驾驶汽车所使用的机器学习软件添加数据集。也就是说，为了获得一项会从我的输入中获得经济利益的自动化服务，我首先必须做一些无偿劳动，帮助提升自动驾驶汽车的性能。

passages.en: Neat, eh? But note also the delicious additional irony that the Captcha is described as an "automated Turing test". The Turing test was conceived, you may recall, as a way of enabling humans to determine whether a machine could respond in such a way that one couldn't tell whether it was a human or a robot. So we have wandered into a world in which machines make us do tricks to prove that we are humans!
passages.zh: 很妙吧？但还要注意其中那种令人回味的额外讽刺：验证码被称为“自动图灵测试”。你可能还记得，图灵测试的构想是让人类能够判断一台机器是否能以某种方式作出回应，使人无法分辨它究竟是人还是机器人。因此，我们已经误入了这样一个世界：机器让我们表演各种把戏，以证明我们是人类！

passages.en: The strangest aspect of this unparalleled shift is how under-discussed it has been. The metaphor of the boiling frog comes to mind. Have we become so subtly conditioned by digital technology that we don't see what's been happening to us? Have we been conditioned to accept a world governed by "smart" tech, trading convenience to the point where we become a bit like machines ourselves?
passages.zh: 这一史无前例的转变最奇怪之处，在于人们几乎没有讨论过它。人们不禁会想到“温水煮青蛙”的比喻。我们是否已经受到数字技术如此悄无声息的影响，以至于看不见它一直在对我们做什么？我们是否已经习惯于接受一个由“智能”技术支配的世界，不断用便利进行交换，直到我们自己也变得有点像机器？

passages.en: In a recent startling and thoughtful book, two scholars — Brett Frischmann, a law professor, and Evan Selinger, a philosopher — argue that the answer to that question is "yes".
passages.zh: 在最近出版的一本令人震撼且发人深省的书中，两位学者——法学教授Brett Frischmann和哲学家Evan Selinger——认为，对这个问题的答案是“是的”。

passages.en: And they're right. There's nothing technophobic(技术恐惧的) about that. We shape our tools and then our tools shape us. Technology is supposed to provide tools that serve human ends. But, as the machine-learning Captcha demonstrates, a significant proportion of digital tech now sees (and uses) humans as means to ends that are not ours. In the process, they reduce us to the status of cheery rats running on treadmills(踏车) designed by people who do not have our interests at heart. So back to the frog metaphor. Are we smart enough to jump out before it's too late? You don't even have to Google it to know the answer.
passages.zh: 他们说得对。这并不意味着技术恐惧。我们塑造工具，然后工具又塑造我们。技术本应提供服务于人类目标的工具。但是，正如机器学习验证码所展示的那样，如今相当大一部分数字技术把人类视为并利用为实现并不属于我们的目标的手段。在这一过程中，它们把我们降低成一群兴高采烈地在跑步机上奔跑的老鼠，而这些跑步机是由那些根本不把我们的利益放在心上的人设计的。所以，让我们回到青蛙的比喻。我们是否足够聪明，能在为时已晚之前跳出去？你甚至不必用Google搜索，也能知道答案。

questions.stem: How did the author respond to the Captcha test?
questions.stem_zh: 作者是如何回应验证码测试的?

options.text: He clicked on the cells randomly.
options.zh: 他随机点击了单元格。

options.text: He accepted the challenge readily.
options.zh: 他欣然接受了挑战。

options.text: He completed it confidently.
options.zh: 他自信地完成了测试。

options.text: He worked on it submissively.
options.zh: 他顺从地完成了测试。

questions.判型: How did the author respond to the Captcha test? 问的是作者在原文里具体做了什么、什么态度，需要回到原文找事实，而不是推断或概括。
questions.拆句: How did the author respond to the Captcha test? 句式平铺直叙，主谓宾清楚，无陷阱。
questions.定位: P2 Like a lamb, I complied, after which the website accepted my input. 我像一只羔羊一样照办了，之后网站接受了我的输入。

locate.en: Like a lamb, I complied, after which the website accepted my input.
locate.zh: 我像一只羔羊一样照办了，之后网站接受了我的输入。

option_analysis.note: clicked on the cells randomly 说作者随机点，但原文 My "challenge" was to click on each cell in the grid that contained a traffic sign. I did so 显示作者是按规则点含交通标志的格子，并不是随机。
accepted the challenge readily 说"欣然接受"，但原文 I did so, a bit irritated 明示作者是带着不快接受的，二者情绪极性相反。
completed it confidently 说"自信地完成"，但原文从未描写作者的信心，只说他不情愿地照办；自信纯属添加。
预判要的就是"顺从地照做"，He worked on it submissively. 是唯一把这层顺从语气保留下来的选项。

questions.stem: What is ironic about the Captcha test?
questions.stem_zh: 验证码测试的讽刺之处是什么?

options.text: A machine can respond to the test as well as humans do.
options.zh: 机器能像人类一样回应测试。

options.text: A machine can outperform humans in object identification.
options.zh: 机器在物体识别方面的表现能超过人类。

options.text: A test designed to test machines is now used by machines to test humans.
options.zh: 一项原本设计用来测试机器的测试现在被机器用来测试人类。

options.text: A test conceived to tell a human from a robot can now do tricks humans can't.
options.zh: 一项原本用于区分人类和机器人的测试现在能做人类做不到的事情。

questions.判型: What is ironic about the Captcha test? 要求回到原文找出作者点明讽刺的那一句，是事实层细节。
questions.拆句: What is ironic about the Captcha test? 结构简单，is 后跟形容词作表语，无陷阱。
questions.定位: P4 But note also the delicious additional irony that the Captcha is described as an "automated Turing test". The Turing test was conceived, you may recall, as a way of enabling humans to determine whether a machine could respond in such a way that one couldn't tell whether it was a human or a robot. So we have wandered into a world in which machines make us do tricks to prove that we are humans! 但还要注意一个绝妙的额外讽刺：Captcha 被称作"自动化的图灵测试"。你或许记得，图灵测试当初的设想，是让人类来判断机器能否做出让人分不清是人还是机器人的回应。结果，我们如今竟漂入了这样一个世界——机器反过来让我们耍把戏，以证明我们是人类！

locate.en: But note also the delicious additional irony that the Captcha is described as an "automated Turing test". The Turing test was conceived, you may recall, as a way of enabling humans to determine whether a machine could respond in such a way that one couldn't tell whether it was a human or a robot. So we have wandered into a world in which machines make us do tricks to prove that we are humans!
locate.zh: 但还要注意一个绝妙的额外讽刺：Captcha 被称作"自动化的图灵测试"。你或许记得，图灵测试当初的设想，是让人类来判断机器能否做出让人分不清是人还是机器人的回应。结果，我们如今竟漂入了这样一个世界——机器反过来让我们耍把戏，以证明我们是人类！

option_analysis.note: A machine can respond to the test as well as humans do 是"机器答得和人一样好"，但原文讽刺的是"角色反转"，不是机器表现优秀。
A machine can outperform humans in object identification 说"机器在物体识别上胜过人类"，但原文没做这种性能比较，纯属添加。
预判要的就是"测机器→测人"的角色反转，A test designed to test machines is now used by machines to test humans. 一句话把这一组对调说清楚。

pairs.orig: The Turing test was conceived, you may recall, as a way of enabling humans to determine whether a machine could respond
pairs.opt: A test designed to test machines

pairs.orig: machines make us do tricks to prove that we are humans
pairs.opt: now used by machines to test humans

option_analysis.note: A test conceived to tell a human from a robot can now do tricks humans can't 说"测试现在能耍出人耍不出的把戏"，主体被换成了"测试"，但原文是 machines make us do tricks——机器让我们耍把戏，主体错位。

questions.stem: Why does the author use the metaphor of the boiling frog?
questions.stem_zh: 作者为什么使用温水煮青蛙的比喻?

options.text: To show that humans are unwilling to trade convenience for control by smart tech.
options.zh: 为了表明人类不愿意用便利换取对智能技术的控制。

options.text: To show that humans are unaware of the potential danger brought by smart tech.
options.zh: 为了表明人类没有意识到智能技术带来的潜在危险。

options.text: To question whether humans are conditioned to accept digital tech.
options.zh: 为了质疑人类是否习惯于接受数字技术。

options.text: To question whether humans are as vulnerable as the boiling frog.
options.zh: 为了质疑人类是否像被煮的青蛙一样脆弱。

questions.判型: Why does the author use the metaphor of the boiling frog? 问的是"作者为什么用"这个比喻，需要从比喻所在语境向上提炼一步作者意图。
questions.拆句: Why does the author use the metaphor of the boiling frog? 标准疑问句结构，of 短语作 metaphor 的后置定语，无陷阱。
questions.定位: P5 The metaphor of the boiling frog comes to mind. Have we become so subtly conditioned by digital technology that we don't see what's been happening to us? 脑海里浮现出"温水煮青蛙"的比喻。我们是不是已经被数字技术悄悄驯化，以至于看不到自己身上正在发生什么？

locate.en: The metaphor of the boiling frog comes to mind. Have we become so subtly conditioned by digital technology that we don't see what's been happening to us?

translation.directions: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to translate a passage from Chinese into English. You should write your answer on Answer Sheet 2.
translation.source_zh: 节俭 (frugality) 是中华民族的传统美德。在中国古代，生产力低下，先人们深知劳动成果来之不易，因而秉持节俭的理念。到了物质极大丰富的今天，中国人民依然坚持节俭的生活方式，体现了理性消费的生活理念和对劳动的尊重。近年来，中国政府持续加强节约型社会的建设，倡导"光盘行动"，减少食物浪费，提倡简约低碳的生活方式，推进资源循环利用，反对过度消费。节约型社会的建设有力地推动了中国经济的高质量发展。
translation.reference_en:
Frugality is a traditional virtue of the Chinese nation. In ancient China, productivity was low, and our ancestors knew well that the fruits of labor did not come easily, so they upheld the idea of frugality. Today, when material wealth is abundant, the Chinese people still maintain a frugal lifestyle, reflecting their concept of rational consumption and their respect for labor. In recent years, the Chinese government has been strengthening the building of a resource-conserving society by advocating the "Clear Your Plate" campaign to reduce food waste, promoting a simple and low-carbon lifestyle, advancing the recycling of resources, and opposing excessive consumption. This building of a resource-conserving society has strongly promoted the high-quality development of China's economy.
【衔接】
第2句句首用时间状语承接"古代"第1句给出总论点"节俭是传统美德"，第2句转入历史佐证，句首 In ancient China 本身就是清晰的时间路标，无需再加连接词，但要确保它紧接第1句、形成"论点→历史依据"的顺承。
第2、3句用today呼应ancient形成古今对照第2句讲 在中国古代、第3句讲 今天，二者是古今对照。第3句句首保留 Today（与上句 ancient China 对仗），读者一眼看出时间从古跳到今，对照逻辑自然显现，不必额外加 however。
第3、4句之间用代词与时间词顺承第3句讲民众坚持、第4句转到政府举措，句首 In recent years 既承接 Today 的时间线，又把视角从"人民"切到"政府"，层次清楚；两句主语不同，不宜用代词合并，保留各自主语反而清晰。
第5句用代词避免重复"节约型社会的建设"第4句末提到 the building of a resource-conserving society，第5句又以同一短语作主语 节约型社会的建设。为减少笨重重复，第5句可用 This/Such efforts 承接：This building of a resource-conserving society 或 These efforts have strongly promoted…，让收尾句更连贯有力。

main_idea.core: 中华节俭美德的文化介绍
main_idea.detail: 全段是一篇典型的中国文化/社会介绍语体，主题是"节俭"。开篇即点题 节俭 (frugality) 是中华民族的传统美德，随后从古代讲到 到了物质极大丰富的今天 再到 近年来 的政府举措，整体在客观陈述一种延续至今的传统与现状，用词偏正式、书面，属四六级汉译英最常见的"中国文化/社会介绍"类。

tense.detail: 全篇主要在客观陈述"节俭是一种延续至今的传统美德、当下中国人仍坚持、政府正持续推进"这类一般性事实与现状，故以一般现在时为基调。只有讲古代背景的那句 在中国古代，生产力低下 例外，需局部改用一般过去时。

term_notes.detail: 节俭 (frugality) 原文已自带英文 frugality，全篇统一沿用 frugality（必要时形容词用 frugal、动词概念用 economize/save），不要中途换成 thrift 又换 frugality，保持一个词。
节约型社会 统一译为 a resource-conserving society（或 a conservation-oriented society）。它在文中出现两次（加强节约型社会的建设 与 节约型社会的建设），两处必须用同一译法，避免前后不一。
"光盘行动" 是文化负载词，直译会让外国读者不懂，宜意译加引号/解释：the "Clear Your Plate" campaign，借后文 减少食物浪费 自然点明其含义即可。

steps.text: 节俭是传统美德（A is B）（主语策略：原句主语）这是一个判断句 节俭 (frugality) 是中华民族的传统美德，骨架就是"A 是 B"：主语 Frugality，系动词 is，表语 a traditional virtue。"中华民族的"作定语修饰 virtue。
"中华民族的"作前置/of定语本句结构简单、无需大改。唯一要安放的是定语 中华民族的：可前置为 a traditional Chinese virtue，或用 of 后置为 a traditional virtue of the Chinese nation，两者皆可，不必照中文堆在名词前。
时态回指全篇基调用一般现在时：is。陈述一个一直成立的事实，不用过去时。 冠词virtue 是可数名词单数，表"一种美德"，前面要加不定冠词 a：a traditional virtue，漏冠词是主体考生高频硬伤。 大小写Frugality 作句首主语首字母大写；表民族的 Chinese 专有形容词任何位置都大写。
Frugality is a traditional virtue of the Chinese nation.
先人们深知…因而秉持…（主语策略：原句主语）这是个含因果的长句。核心主语是 先人们（our ancestors），两个并列谓语动作是"深知"(knew well) 和"秉持"(upheld)，由 因而 连成因果。开头的 在中国古代，生产力低下 是背景，不进主干、作状语处理。

背景作状语+从句+因果连接把三段降级安放：① 在中国古代→时间状语 In ancient China；② 生产力低下→可作伴随背景，用 with productivity being low 或独立分句 productivity was low；③ 劳动成果来之不易→作 knew 的宾语从句 that the fruits of labor did not come easily；④ 因而→so/and therefore 引出结果。避免照中文用四个"逗号+动词"平铺成流水句。

时态偏离全篇基调：本句讲 在中国古代 的事，是已经过去的历史，全部动词用一般过去时——was low/knew/did not come/upheld，不能用现在时。这是本篇唯一的时态例外，要特别警觉。 单复数"先人们"是复数：our ancestors（复数 + 复数谓语）。"劳动成果"宜用复数 the fruits of labor。 短语搭配"来之不易"译 did not come easily/were hard-won；"秉持……理念"用 upheld the idea/value of frugality，搭配 uphold/embrace 比生硬的 hold 地道。
In ancient China, productivity was low, and our ancestors knew well that the fruits of labor did not come easily, so they upheld the idea of frugality.
中国人民依然坚持…（主语策略：原句主语）主语是 中国人民（the Chinese people），核心谓语是 依然坚持（still maintain/adhere to），宾语是 节俭的生活方式（a frugal lifestyle）。后半的 体现了…… 是这种坚持带来的结果/补充说明，不抢主干。

"体现了…"用现在分词作状语把两处降级：① 到了物质极大丰富的今天→时间状语 Today, when material wealth is abundant（或 In today's age of material abundance）；② 体现了理性消费的生活理念和对劳动的尊重→用现在分词短语 reflecting their concept of rational consumption and their respect for labor，作伴随状语挂在主干后，比再起一个并列谓语更地道，也避免缺主语。

时态回到全篇基调一般现在时：maintain/adhere、reflecting。本句讲 今天 的现状，正合现在时。 主谓一致the Chinese people 表"人民、人们"作复数，谓语用原形 maintain/adhere（不加 s）；分词逻辑主语也是 people，物主代词用 their。 单复数与冠词lifestyle 可数，表"一种生活方式"用 a frugal lifestyle；consumption/labor/respect 此处是抽象不可数名词，不加 a、不加复数。
Today, when material wealth is abundant, the Chinese people still maintain a frugal lifestyle, reflecting their concept of rational consumption and their respect for labor.
政府持续加强建设（领起多个并列动作）（主语策略：原句主语）主语是 中国政府（the Chinese government），主干谓语取最核心的 持续加强节约型社会的建设（has been strengthening the building of a resource-conserving society）。后面 倡导"光盘行动" 等一连串动作都是"加强建设"的具体举措，不是平级新句。

一串动作打包成by doing方式状语把 倡导"光盘行动"，减少食物浪费，提倡简约低碳的生活方式，推进资源循环利用，反对过度消费 这五个并列动作，统一降级为 by + 动名词的方式状语：by advocating the "Clear Your Plate" campaign to reduce food waste, promoting a simple and low-carbon lifestyle, advancing the recycling of resources, and opposing excessive consumption。其中"减少食物浪费"是"光盘行动"的目的，用 to reduce 不定式挂上去，逻辑更紧。这样避免六个 and 堆成超长流水句。

时态近年来 + 持续 表示从过去延续到现在并仍在进行，宜用现在完成进行时 has been strengthening（用一般现在时 strengthens 亦可接受）。这是"近年来"的标志性时态，不要用一般过去时。 主谓一致the Chinese government 是单数集体名词，谓语用 has been/strengthens（单数）；与第3句 people 的复数谓语区分开。 动名词并列形态by 后所有动作必须统一为动名词 -ing 形式（advocating/promoting/advancing/opposing），不能 by 后混进原形或 to do，并列项形式要一致。 单复数campaign 特指"光盘行动"用 the；food waste/consumption 抽象不可数不加复数；resources 表"各类资源"用复数。

In recent years, the Chinese government has been strengthening the building of a resource-conserving society by advocating the "Clear Your Plate" campaign to reduce food waste, promoting a simple and low-carbon lifestyle, advancing the recycling of resources, and opposing excessive consumption.
建设推动了发展（主语策略：原句主语）主语是 节约型社会的建设（the building of a resource-conserving society），谓语 有力地推动了（has strongly promoted），宾语 中国经济的高质量发展（the high-quality development of China's economy）。是清晰的"主语—推动—宾语"结构。
两处"…的"均用of短语后置本句是简单句，无需大拆。两处长定语都用 of 后置：节约型社会的建设→the building of a resource-conserving society；中国经济的高质量发展→the high-quality development of China's economy。"有力地"作副词 strongly 修饰谓语。

时态"推动了"含已产生的结果且延续至今，用现在完成时 has promoted 最贴；回指基调用一般现在时 promotes 亦可。主语 the building 单数，助动词用 has。 主谓一致主语中心词是 building（单数），谓语用 has promoted/promotes（单数），别被后面的 society 带偏成复数。 搭配与名词"高质量发展"用 high-quality development（high-quality 作复合形容词加连字符）；development、economy 此处不可数/特指，development 不加复数、economy 用 China's 限定。
The building of a resource-conserving society has strongly promoted the high-quality development of China's economy.
